messages.author: 0beedbaa451f0901
messages.subject: Noob ggplot question
parts:
Hi!

I was wondering if it was possible to use 2 data frame as the "data" in the ggplot command, please.

Here is what I did:


+ > lildia.df <- diamonds[1:100,]
> stuff.df <- data.frame(dogs=(rnorm(100)))
> ggplot(data=c(lildia.df,stuff.df),geom_point(aes(x=lildia.df$carat,y=stuff.df$dogs)))
Error in ggplot.data.frame(fortify(data, ...), mapping) :
  Mapping should be created with aes or aes_string
>

Is this simply not possible, please?

Thanks,
Erin

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: Noob ggplot question
parts:
I don't think so. You can, however, construct a new data.frame and use that.

ggplot(df1, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_point(data = df2, aes(x, y)) # another df here

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: Noob ggplot question
parts:
Hi,

Since your two data.frames have the same number of rows, you can combine them with cbind(),

d = cbind(diamonds[1:100,], data.frame(dogs=(rnorm(100))))

and then use these data (note: no $ in ggplot2)

ggplot(d, aes(x = carat, y = dogs)) + geom_point()


HTH,

b.

messages.author: 139553f03a0e344d
messages.subject: Re: Noob ggplot question
parts:
Hey Erin,

To elaborate slightly, ggplot constructs graphics in layers. Each layer essentially draws from one dataset. So, depending on what you want to do, you can either merge data.frames into one for display in a single layer (the solution described by baptiste) or you can add more layers to your graph, each drawn from a different data.frame (the solution described by Roman).

Warm regards,
Brian
